figures.title: This paper in the 13 components, against the field
figures.subtitle: Each box: what this paper does, then common practice across all sensors and how many ledger papers share it.
figures.caption: Verdicts compare the paper's choice for each component with common practice across 8,995 ledger entries on any sensor (silent speech, brain-to-text, lip reading), not only audio-visual papers.

M01.note: Inherited from the WLAS/LRS lineage; nothing to compare.

M02.note: Automatic subtitle labels as in LRS; standard for broadcast-derived data.

M03.field: Pretraining and noise augmentation are common
M03.note: The curriculum is inherited from WLAS in near-identical wording, and the non-public MV-LRS pretraining is an uncontrolled part of the reported gain.

M04.note: Inherited; ordinary voiced broadcast speech at test.

M06.field: One loss per system; joint CTC/attention in current work
M06.note: Standard: a concurrent same-group paper already compared CTC with a Transformer, this comparison confounds loss with beam, LM weight and fusion, and joint CTC/attention has since made the either/or question moot.

M07.note: Standard external character LM with shallow fusion; it closes most of the CTC vs seq2seq gap.

M09.note: Offline benchmark study; no confirmation step.

M10.note: Offline benchmark study; no correction step.

M11.field: In-the-wild sentence test sets; speaker-disjoint only in some
M11.note: Not reported: speaker count and train/test overlap are absent, so LRS2-BBC results do not establish unseen-speaker performance.

M12.field: Repeated runs or variance where differences are small
M12.note: Not reported: single runs, and the 8.2% vs 8.5% clean audio-visual gap is within about 0.34 pt binomial error.

M13.note: Compute is reported but inconsistently (GPU model differs between sections), and the numbers depend on non-public MV-LRS.
